3. Critical path: A-C-F-I-J-K (Path 4) – the longest path through the network diagram; every activity on it has TS = FS = 0. It takes 16 days.
4. Shortest possible time: 16 days.
5. E, G and H – the activities with free slack FS > 0 (E = 2, G = 1, H = 4 days); every other activity has FS = 0. FS = (min ES of successors) – EF: E may finish as late as day 8 (H and I also wait for F), G day 13 (J waits for I), H day 14 (K waits for J).
6. B, D, E, G and H – the activities with total slack TS > 0 (B = 2, D = 1, E = 2, G = 1, H = 4 days). TS = LS – ES: a delay within the TS leaves the project finish date (day 16) unchanged; A, C, F, I, J, K are critical (TS = 0).
7. Choice 1 (delayed for at least 1 day). B has ES = 2, LS = 4, TS = 2 days (day numbers on the same scale as ES/LS: B normally starts on day 2). Starting on day 5 delays B by 3 days, 1 day more than its total slack: B 5–7, E 7–9, I 9–14, J 14–15, K 15–17. The project finishes on day 17 instead of 16, at least 1 day late (A-B-E-I-J-K becomes the critical path).
8. Choice 2 (not affected). H has ES = 8, LS = 12, TS = 4 days (FS = 4). Starting on day 10 delays H by 2 days, within its total slack: H finishes on day 12, still before the early start of K on day 14 (K must also wait for J, EF = 14), so K and the project finish date (day 16) are unchanged.
9. Choice 3 (affects G but not J). D has ES = 2, LS = 3, TS = 1, FS = 0. Starting on day 3 delays D by 1 day: D finishes on day 7, so the early start of G moves from day 6 to 7 – G is affected (G 7–13, its slack is used up). J waits for G (EF 13) and I (EF 13), so its early start stays day 13: J and the project finish date (day 16) are not affected.
